transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up time from someone who needs it more, but... well, I guess I'm here because things have been just a little difficult lately at school. 

I'm a teacher, and the district recently put this new bilingual social-emotional learning rollout on my plate, right on top of my regular teaching schedule. Which is a wonderful initiative, really, I'm so glad we're doing it. But... I don't know, I still get through the day just fine, but I've been feeling a bit wound up and, well, maybe a little discouraged lately? In a way that really isn't like me at all. 

I'm usually very organized, but I've actually started putting off my lesson plans and ignoring emails that I used to handle without a second thought. I feel awful even admitting that out loud, honestly, because I know I should be able to balance it. I just want to get back to doing a good job for my students. Does that make sense, or... is that the sort of thing you help with?
Have you noticed that you’re not enjoying things that you usually like to do, like teaching or other activities?

Oh, gosh, no, I hope I didn't make it sound like I don't want to teach anymore! I still really love it. The kids are just wonderful, and being in the classroom with them is still such a joy for me. 

And outside of school, I... well, I still enjoy my usual weekend activities, for the most part. It's really just that overwhelmed feeling when I have to sit down and do the extra planning or answer those emails. I haven't lost my passion for the things I love, I promise. I hope that makes sense? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you noticed that you feel tired or have been lacking energy more often than usual, even when you haven’t been doing anything particularly strenuous?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I've been lacking energy. I mean... I get a little tired by Friday afternoon, but I think every teacher does, right? But no, I haven't been feeling physically exhausted or drained out of nowhere. 

I still have plenty of energy for my classes and my day-to-day routine. I really try to take good care of myself and get enough sleep so I can be at my best for everyone. I'm definitely not just, you know, lying on the couch all day or anything like that! It's really just that mental block when it comes to the new rollout paperwork. 

Am I explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
Do you find yourself feeling persistently worried or tense, even when there isn’t an immediate deadline or task pressing on you?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I'm really not a... well, a nervous person by nature. When I'm at home or on the weekends, I can relax just fine. 

It's really only when I'm sitting at my desk and I see that new curriculum binder, or when I know I have to tackle those emails I've been putting off. That's when I get that little knot of tension. But if there's nothing pressing right in front of me? No, I feel completely normal. 

I hope that's a good sign? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the clearest picture possible.
When you sit down to work on the new curriculum or related tasks, do you find yourself actively avoiding thinking about it or trying to push it out of your mind?

Oh, well... I wouldn't say I actively try to push it out of my mind, exactly. I mean, I know it's important, and I really do want to do a good job with it. 

It's more like... I just find other things that need doing first. You know how it is in a classroom, there's always a bulletin board to fix or a student's project to look over. I guess I just prioritize those things, and then the curriculum stuff sort of... gets pushed to the end of the day. I'm not intentionally ignoring it! I just want to make sure my students have what they need first. 

Is that normal? I mean, I hope that doesn't make me sound irresponsible or anything. I really am trying my best to manage it all.

Have these feelings around the new curriculum and emails caused any problems in other areas of your life, like with your relationships, your performance in the classroom, or anything else that’s important to you?

Oh, goodness, no, my relationships at home are wonderful. And my classroom... well, I'm definitely still teaching and meeting all my basic responsibilities. The kids always come first, and I make sure they get my absolute best! 

But... I suppose, if I'm being completely honest... I *have* missed or, well, pushed back a couple of the new planning deadlines. And... I've actually needed a few reminders from my colleagues lately for some administrative tasks that I usually complete really reliably on my own. 

I feel a little embarrassed even admitting that. I really don't want anyone to think I'm not doing my fair share, because I'm usually so on top of things! I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad teacher? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right information.
Have you noticed any trouble concentrating, making decisions, or thinking clearly when you're trying to work on the new curriculum or other tasks lately?

Oh, um... well, no, not really. I mean, I wouldn't say I have trouble thinking clearly or anything like that. When I'm teaching, I'm completely focused on the kids, and I know exactly what I'm doing. 

When I finally sit down with the new curriculum stuff... I suppose I do sometimes find myself reading the same paragraph a couple of times before it really sinks in. But I think that's just because the new material is a bit dense, you know? It's not that I can't concentrate, it just takes a little more effort to sort through all the new guidelines and figure out how they want us to implement them. 

I'm sure everyone takes a little time to adjust to new materials, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing it exactly the way they want us to, so I guess I just take my time with it. Does that sound like a normal reaction to you?
When you're faced with working on the new curriculum or related tasks, do you ever feel anxious about whether you're doing it right or worry that your work won’t meet expectations?

Oh, well... no, I wouldn't say I feel anxious, exactly. Anxious is such a strong word, isn't it? 

I just... I care a great deal about my work. I've been doing this for a long time, and I've always prided myself on being very thorough. So, when I look at the new curriculum, I just want to be absolutely sure I'm interpreting their new standards correctly. It's more of a... a healthy desire to be accurate, I think. 

I mean, nobody wants to put together a whole week of lesson plans only to find out they missed the mark on the new district guidelines, right? So I just want to be careful. I hope that just shows that I'm dedicated to doing a good job. That's a good thing, isn't it?
When it comes to working on the new curriculum tasks, do you find yourself avoiding sitting down to start them because it feels overwhelming or unpleasant?

Oh, well... no, I wouldn't say I avoid them. I mean, I always get my work done! 

It's just that... well, you know how it is when you have a lot on your plate. Sometimes I just... prioritize other things first. Like, I'll make sure my classroom is perfectly organized, or I'll spend a little extra time responding to parents' emails, because those feel so immediate and important. 

And then, by the time I get to the new curriculum planning... well, sometimes it's just a bit late in the day, and I'm tired. So it might look like I'm putting it off, but really, I'm just making sure all my other ducks are in a row first. It's just good time management to handle the immediate needs of the students first, don't you think? I certainly wouldn't say I find it overwhelming... just a matter of scheduling, really.

When you're working on other tasks instead of starting the new curriculum planning, does it feel like it's because you're trying to avoid the uncomfortable feelings that come up when you think about that work?

Oh, goodness, no. I really don't think it's about uncomfortable feelings at all. 

I mean, I love my job, and I genuinely enjoy doing all those other things for my classroom. When I'm organizing the reading corner or grading papers, I just feel like I'm being productive and taking care of my students. I certainly don't feel like I'm running away from the curriculum or trying to dodge anything negative. 

It's really just about wanting to be as helpful and responsible as possible in the moment. You understand how busy a classroom can get, right? I just try to keep everything running smoothly so the kids have the best environment possible. I hope that just shows that I'm keeping my students as my number one priority... that's the right way to handle it, isn't it?

When you're not working on the new curriculum and choosing to do other tasks instead, does it feel more like you're not interested or don’t feel like doing the curriculum work, rather than just prioritizing other things?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I mean... I'm very interested in the curriculum! I've always loved teaching, and I've never been one to just... lose interest or not feel like doing my job. I'd hate for you to think I'm just slacking off or being lazy about it. 

It truly is just about making sure everything else is taken care of first. The children just need so much day-to-day support, and I want to be there for them. I'm still very dedicated to my profession... I really am. I hope you can see that I'm just trying to be a responsible teacher. That makes sense, doesn't it?
When you think about starting the new curriculum planning, do you ever feel a strong sense of dislike or want to steer clear of it, even if just for a little while?

Oh, well... no, I wouldn't use words like "dislike" or say I want to steer clear of it. That makes it sound like I'm being resistant or difficult, and I certainly don't want to be that kind of teacher. 

I mean, I suppose sometimes when I think about sitting down with all the new binders and standards, I might feel a little... hesitant? Just because it's a lot to take in, and I want to make sure I do it exactly right for the students. So maybe I just pause for a moment before diving in. But I definitely don't have a strong dislike for it. I'm always willing to learn new things for my classroom. That's a normal way to feel when something is brand new, right? I'm just trying to be careful and thorough.
When you're putting off the curriculum planning, is it because you're worried that your work won’t be perfect or up to your usual standards?

Oh... no, I don't think it's that. I mean, I certainly hold myself to a high standard—I think all good teachers do! But I wouldn't say I'm sitting there worrying that my work won't be perfect. 

I've been doing this for quite a few years now, and I feel very confident in my ability to put together a solid curriculum once I'm, you know, fully focused on it. It's really just about making sure I'm giving my current students everything they need right this second. I just want to be as helpful as I can be in the present moment. 

I hope it doesn't sound like I'm doubting my own abilities or anything like that. I just always want to do a good job for the kids, and sometimes that means tackling the immediate things first. That's the most important thing, wouldn't you agree?
When you think about working on the new curriculum planning, do you ever feel like it’s too much to handle or that you’re not sure where to even begin?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say it's too much to handle at all. I mean, I've handled plenty of new initiatives over the years, and I've always managed just fine. I certainly wouldn't want you to think I'm overwhelmed or incompetent, because I'm not. 

I suppose... well, maybe I just haven't quite decided on the absolute best starting point yet. There are a lot of new materials, and I just want to make sure I approach it in the most organized way possible. So I might be taking a little extra time to just... map it out in my head before I actually sit down and start writing. But I definitely know how to begin, and I don't feel like I can't handle it. 

I'm just trying to be very thoughtful about the process so the transition is smooth for the students. That's a good approach to take, right? I just want to make sure I'm doing things the right way.
When you finally do sit down to work on the new curriculum planning, do you find that getting started feels unusually difficult or that it takes a lot more effort than it used to?

Oh, goodness, no. I wouldn't say it's unusually difficult to get started once I'm actually sitting there. I certainly don't want to give the impression that I'm... you know, losing my touch or struggling to do my job! 

Once I finally have my materials out and I'm at my desk, I just get right to work. I mean, sure, it takes a normal amount of focus to dive into a brand new set of standards, but it definitely doesn't take more effort than it used to. I've always been a very dedicated worker, and I still am. 

I think it just takes a moment to get into the rhythm of the new format, which is pretty standard for any teacher facing a big change, wouldn't you say? I'm just doing my best to adapt gracefully, and once I start typing, it all flows just fine.

When you finally do sit down to work on the new curriculum planning, do you ever notice yourself feeling a sense of emotional discomfort or resistance, even if just at the very beginning, before you get into the work?

Oh, no, I wouldn't call it emotional discomfort. That sounds so... serious, doesn't it? I certainly wouldn't want you to think I'm sitting there feeling upset or resistant about doing my job. 

I mean, maybe there's just a tiny, fleeting moment of... oh, I don't know, just adjusting gears? Like when you go from a warm room out into the cold, it just takes a second to catch your breath. But it's really nothing I'd call resistance. I'm always very willing to do what needs to be done for my classroom. 

I think anyone would feel just a little bit of a shift when starting something brand new, right? It's perfectly normal to take a deep breath before diving into a big project. I just want to be sure I'm in the right headspace to do a good job for the students.
Have you been feeling guilty or overly critical of yourself about the delays in working on the new curriculum, even though you know you’re still doing a good job overall?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I feel guilty or overly critical. I mean, I certainly don't sit around beating myself up or anything like that. I've always held myself to a high standard, of course, but I'm not... I'm not punishing myself over it. 

I suppose I might just have a passing thought here or there, wishing I was a tiny bit further along, but that's just because I care so much about being prepared for the kids. I think it's perfectly natural for any dedicated teacher to want to be ahead of schedule, don't you? 

I just remind myself that I'm doing my best and that I'm taking the time to do it right. I'm definitely not being too hard on myself, though. I'm just trying to be responsible and thorough. That's a good way to look at it, isn't it?
Have you noticed any loss of interest or pleasure in activities you used to enjoy, like hobbies or time with friends and family, not just in your work tasks?

Oh, goodness, no. I'm still very much enjoying my life outside of school. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just... sitting at home feeling sorry for myself or anything like that. 

I still love my weekend gardening, and I always look forward to Sunday dinners with my family. I mean, maybe I'm a tiny bit more tired by the time Friday rolls around, so I might opt for a quiet evening in instead of going out, but that's just normal for someone my age, isn't it? 

I'm still very active and involved with the things I love. I think it's so important to keep up with your hobbies to be a well-rounded teacher, don't you agree? I'm definitely still finding plenty of joy in my day-to-day life.
Have you found that even the things you usually enjoy, like your gardening or time with family, don't bring you as much pleasure as they used to?

Oh, well, like I think I just mentioned a moment ago... no, I really haven't lost any joy in those things at all. I hope I didn't make it sound otherwise just now? I wouldn't want to give you the wrong impression. 

I know you have to ask these things to be thorough, but I really do still get so much out of being out in the dirt with my plants, and seeing my family is always the highlight of my week. I promise I'm not sitting around feeling empty or anything like that. The pleasure is absolutely still there for me. That's a good sign, isn't it? That I'm still really looking forward to my Sunday routines?
When you think about the new curriculum planning, do you ever feel a lack of motivation or interest in starting it, even when you know there’s nothing else more urgent to do?

Well, I suppose... I mean, I did come in today because, well, ever since the district decided to add this new bilingual social-emotional learning rollout to my plate—on top of my regular teaching, of course—I've just felt a little... off. 

I'm still getting through the day, naturally, and the kids are well taken care of, but I do feel a bit more wound up and, I don't know, maybe a tiny bit discouraged? It's really not like me. And I guess I have noticed that I've started putting off the new lesson plans, and even some emails that I used to just handle right away without a second thought. 

It's just that I want to make sure I do it perfectly, you know? It's not that I don't care. I'm just taking my time to process it all. That makes sense, doesn't it? That a big change like that might make someone hesitate just a little before diving in?
